text:
alex: Heads-up — planning a guided backfill for analytics.users to populate the new usage_score column. Target change window tonight 01:00-03:00 UTC. Need a rate-limit + canary plan to avoid long locks. @maria can you sanity-check the approach?

maria: Sounds reasonable. Quick Q: table size and whether the migration added the column with a default? we should avoid full-table rewrite.

alex: Table ~180M rows. We added the column as nullable earlier this week so no rewrite. Backfill will only update usage_score. Plan: chunk by id ranges, 4 parallel workers, throttle writes. Avoid big single UPDATE txs.

sam: Consider using a batched upsert job (COPY to temp then update) to cut down WAL churn. Also check pgbouncer max_conns and replica capacity.

julia: To reduce lock risk keep transactions < 30s per chunk and increase checkpoint_timeout a bit. Index creation should be CONCURRENTLY after majority of rows are updated.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled by @alex for 2025-11-12T01:00:00Z. Canary step required: canary_count=5_000_000 rows, then 30m observation before ramp.

alex: Canary ACK. I'll run a QA canary at 22:30 UTC first. Will pin worker image to analytics/backfill:v1.8.3 to freeze behavior.

maria: Proposed rate settings: --batch-size=5000 --sleep-ms=200 --parallel=4 (roughly ~1000 rows/s). That keeps CPU+IO sane.

sam: Add operational abort rules: if replica_lag > 10s or disk usage > 85% then stop. Also monitor WAL send/replication.

julia: Index plan: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_usage_score ON analytics.users (usage_score) WHERE usage_score IS NOT NULL; schedule after traffic ramps down (02:00-04:00 UTC).

alex: I'll draft a 1-pager runbook with commands and rollback steps. Rollback = stop jobs, revert external pointers, keep column as-is (no destructive DDL).

ops-bot: Created incident channel #inc-189 and granted write for on-call. Notifying on-call now.

sam: I'll be on-call for the window. Will watch replica lag and pg_stat_activity for long queries. Add statement_timeout=60000 for worker connections to limit runaway queries.

maria: Also recommend setting application-level idempotency key and a schema flag file so we don't accidentally re-run the same ranges.

alex: Great — final checklist: QA canary at 22:30, scheduled run 01:00, canary -> pause -> ramp, index concurrently after. I'll post the runbook + exact job command before 23:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
